audioText: W: Hello! I'm Li Hua. What's your name? M: Hi, Li Hua. I'm Tom. Nice to meet you!
q: What is the boy's name?

audioText: W: Anna, where are you from? M: I'm from Germany. I can speak German and English.
q: Where is Anna from?

audioText: M: My hobby is playing the guitar. What about you? W: I love reading books.
q: What is the girl's hobby?

audioText: W: My elder brother is an engineer. He is very clever. M: Sounds great!
q: What is the woman's brother's job?

audioText: W: What time do you get up, Tom? M: I always get up at six thirty.
q: What time does Tom get up?

audioText: W: How do you go to school, Amy? M: I go to school on foot.
q: How does Amy go to school?

audioText: W: When does school end? M: It ends at four thirty in the afternoon.
q: When does school end?

audioText: W: Do you often play table tennis after school? M: Yes, every day with my friends.
q: How often does the boy play table tennis?

audioText: M: The Earth is our home. We must protect it. We can recycle paper and plastic.
q: What does the speaker say about the Earth?

audioText: W: Don't throw waste on the ground, please. M: Sorry, I will put it in the bin.
q: What will the boy do?
options: put the waste in the bin

audioText: M: There are many forests and oceans on the Earth. Animals live in them.
q: Where do animals live?

audioText: W: We should turn off the tap when we brush our teeth. It saves water.
q: What does the woman suggest?
explain: turn off the tap → save water

audioText: W: Look outside! It's raining. M: Let's stay at home and read books.
q: What is the weather like?

audioText: M: I love summer. We can swim in the sea. W: Me too!
q: What does the boy love about summer?
explain: We can swim in the sea.

audioText: W: In autumn, leaves turn yellow and fall. I love this season.
q: When do leaves turn yellow?

audioText: M: It's snowing! Let's put on our scarves and gloves.
q: What will they wear?

audioText: W: One day, we will travel to the Moon by rocket. I can't wait!
q: How will they travel to the Moon?

audioText: M: There is no air on the Moon. We must wear spacesuits to breathe.
q: Why do astronauts wear spacesuits on the Moon?
explain: No air → must wear spacesuits to breathe.

audioText: W: I want to be an astronaut. I love science and space. M: That's a great dream.
q: What does the girl want to be?
explain: I want to be an astronaut.

audioText: M: The Moon is about 384,000 kilometres from the Earth.
q: How far is the Moon from the Earth?

audioText: W: Beijing is the capital of China. The Great Wall is there. M: I want to visit it!
q: What is the capital of China?
explain: Beijing is the capital of China.

audioText: M: Tokyo is a very modern city in Japan. Tokyo Tower is famous.
q: Where is Tokyo?

audioText: W: Bangkok has many old palaces and delicious Thai food.
q: What does Bangkok have?

audioText: M: Xi'an is an ancient capital of China. It has the Terracotta Army.
q: What famous site is in Xi'an?

audioText: W: Every Friday afternoon we can join different clubs. I will join the Music Club.
q: Which club will the girl join?
explain: I will join the Music Club.

audioText: M: I can draw very well. I want to join the Art Club.
q: Which club does the boy want to join?

audioText: W: Chess makes you think fast. We have a school chess game every year.
q: How often is the school chess game held?

audioText: M: Our Science Club is building a robot called Star. It can say 'Hello'.
q: What can the robot do?

audioText: W: My hobby is collecting stamps. I have more than 300 stamps.
q: How many stamps does the girl have?

audioText: M: The 1980 red monkey stamp is very valuable. It is my favourite.
q: Which stamp is the boy's favourite?

audioText: W: Grandpa told me: never touch stamps with dirty hands.
q: What did grandpa say?
explain: never touch with dirty hands → 保持手干净

audioText: M: I like sharing my collection with my friends. It makes me happy.
q: Why does the boy share his collection?

audioText: W: How long have you known Amy? M: I have known her since childhood. We are best friends.
q: How long has the boy known Amy?
explain: I have known her since childhood.

audioText: W: I lost my wallet at the market yesterday. M: Don't worry. Here is some money for the bus.
q: What did the girl lose at the market?

audioText: W: Do you think true friends should share secrets? M: Yes, and they should support each other in difficult times.
q: What should true friends do according to the boy?
options: Support each other in difficult times
explain: support each other in difficult times.

audioText: W: Is it safe to give your phone number to online friends? M: No, never give your real address or phone number to strangers.
q: What should you never give to strangers online?
options: Your real address or phone number
explain: never give your real address or phone number.

audioText: W: How was your trip to London? M: It was great! The flight took eleven hours from Guangzhou.
q: How long was the flight from Guangzhou to London?

audioText: W: What did you visit in London? M: We went to the British Museum and saw many old Chinese treasures.
q: What did they see at the British Museum?

audioText: W: Did you enjoy the food in London? M: Yes, I loved the fish and chips, but I missed Chinese rice.
q: What food did the boy miss?

audioText: W: What should I pack for a trip abroad? M: Bring a jacket, comfortable shoes and a power adapter. And check your passport!
q: What three things does the boy suggest packing?
explain: a jacket, comfortable shoes and a power adapter.

audioText: W: What happened to that little dog on the street? M: He was wet, cold and hungry. My dad carried him home.
q: What was the dog like when they found him?

audioText: W: Can your dog Lucky open the door? M: Yes! He can shake hands, sit and even open the door.
q: What can Lucky do?
options: Shake hands, sit and open the door
explain: shake hands, sit and even open the door.

audioText: W: Pandas are protected by law now. M: Yes, the government has built many panda reserves.
q: What has the government built for pandas?

audioText: W: How many wild pandas are there now? M: Over 1,800. They are no longer endangered!
q: How many wild pandas were there in 2021?

audioText: W: Why are trees so important? M: They give us oxygen and clean the air. Some trees can live for thousands of years.
q: How long can some trees live?

audioText: W: What will happen if we keep cutting down trees? M: If we keep cutting, deserts will grow bigger and bigger.
q: What will happen if we keep cutting trees?

audioText: W: When is Tree Planting Day in China? M: Every March 12th. Students plant young trees everywhere.
q: When is Tree Planting Day?

audioText: W: How can we help trees every day? M: Use both sides of paper and recycle old books and boxes.
q: What is one way to help trees every day?
explain: use both sides of the paper.

audioText: W: Why is there no water this morning? M: The water pipes are being repaired. No water until evening.
q: Why is there no water?

audioText: W: How did you brush your teeth without running water? M: I used a small bottle of water.
q: How did the boy brush his teeth?
options: He used a small bottle of water
He went to a friend's house

audioText: W: How much did the bottle of water cost? M: It cost 5 yuan. Every drop of water is precious now.
q: How much did the bottle of water cost?

audioText: W: How can we save water at home? M: Take showers instead of baths, and fix leaking taps quickly.
q: What is one way to save water at home?

audioText: W: What happened last Friday evening? M: There was a big storm and all the lights went out.
q: What caused the power to go out?

audioText: W: What did your dad do when the lights went out? M: He found some candles and lit them one by one.
q: What did Dad do to bring light?

audioText: W: When did the power come back? M: At midnight. I saw many messages from my friends then.
q: When did the power come back?

audioText: W: Where does clean energy come from? M: Solar power, wind power and water power. They don't pollute the air.
q: Name one type of clean energy mentioned.
explain: solar power, wind power and water power.

audioText: W: Who wrote Quiet Night Thoughts? M: Li Bai, a great Chinese poet. The poem has only four lines.
q: How many lines does Quiet Night Thoughts have?

audioText: W: What does the moonlight look like in the poem? M: It looks like frost on the floor.
q: What does the moonlight look like in the poem?

audioText: W: Can anyone write a poem? M: Yes! Choose a feeling, think of images, and write three or four short lines.
q: What is the first step to write a poem?

audioText: W: What does the river do in the student's poem? M: It whispers softly at night. The moon is round and stars are bright.
q: What does the river do in the poem?

audioText: W: Who is Chef Liu? M: He is a famous cook in Guangzhou. Cooking was just his hobby twenty years ago.
q: What was cooking for Chef Liu twenty years ago?

audioText: W: When did Chef Liu first try cooking? M: He fried his first egg at the age of eight. He burned it!
q: What happened when Chef Liu first fried an egg?

audioText: W: Where is Chef Liu's restaurant now? M: It is in a five-star hotel, and he also teaches young cooks on TV.
q: Where is Chef Liu's restaurant now?

audioText: W: What advice does Chef Liu give? M: Start from what you love. A hobby today can be your career tomorrow. But you need passion and practice.
q: What does Chef Liu say you need besides passion?

audioText: W: What did you learn from the encyclopaedia? M: I learned that the moon is 384,000 kilometres from the Earth, and there's no air on it.
q: How far is the moon from the Earth?

audioText: W: Can you find a topic quickly in an encyclopaedia? M: Yes, use the index at the end of the book.
q: How can you find a topic quickly in an encyclopaedia?
options: Use the index at the end
explain: use the index at the end.

audioText: W: Who wrote the oldest encyclopaedia? M: A Roman writer called Pliny, about 2,000 years ago. He wrote 37 volumes.
q: How many volumes did Pliny write?

audioText: W: Is Wikipedia reliable? M: Not everything on the Internet is true. Always check more than one website before believing.
q: What should you do before believing online information?

audioText: W: How many basic digits do we have? M: Ten — from zero to nine. With these we can write any number.
q: How many basic digits are there?

audioText: W: Where did the ten-digit system come from? M: It came from ancient India, not from Greece or Rome.
q: Where did the ten-digit number system come from?

audioText: W: Can you say 1,500,000 in English? M: Sure. One million five hundred thousand.
q: How do you say 1,500,000 in English?

audioText: W: Who invented zero? M: Ancient Indian mathematicians. The Greeks had no zero at all.
q: Who invented zero?

audioText: W: When did you get your first computer? M: Last year, for my thirteenth birthday. It was a small laptop, only 1.5 kilograms.
q: How old was the boy when he got the computer?

audioText: W: How do you give instructions for using a computer? M: Use the imperative: Turn on the computer. Open the program. Save the file.
q: What form is used to give instructions?

audioText: W: What is Rule 1 for Internet safety? M: Keep your password secret. Never tell anyone, even your best friend.
q: Should you tell your best friend your password?

audioText: W: How often should you change your password? M: Every few months, to stay safe on the Internet.
q: How often should you change your password?

audioText: W: What are the Four Great Inventions of ancient China? M: Paper, the compass, printing and gunpowder. Each changed the world.
q: How many great inventions are mentioned?

audioText: W: Who invented the light bulb? M: Edison invented it. So we say 'The light bulb was invented by Edison.'
q: How do we express this in passive voice?
options: The light bulb was invented by Edison
The light bulb invent by Edison

audioText: W: Who was Louis Braille? M: A boy who lost his sight at three. He invented a writing system using small dots.
q: At what age did Braille lose his sight?

audioText: W: What can we learn from young inventors? M: Even young people and those with difficulties can invent great things that change the world.
q: What does Braille's story teach us?
options: Even young people with difficulties can invent great things
explain: even young people with difficulties can invent.

audioText: W: How can I remember new words better? M: Repeat them after one hour, one day, and one week. It really helps.
q: When should you review new words?
options: After one hour, one day and one week
explain: one hour, one day and one week.

audioText: W: What is the best way to understand something deeply? M: Teach it to someone else. When you explain, you understand it better.
q: What helps you understand something better?

audioText: W: How strong is your memory? M: The memory is like a muscle — the more you train it, the stronger it grows.
q: What does the speaker compare memory to?

audioText: W: How many numbers can a memory champion remember? M: Alex Mullen can remember 3,000 random numbers in one hour. Amazing!
q: How many numbers can Alex Mullen remember in one hour?

audioText: W: Who is the Monkey King? M: Sun Wukong, a hero born from a stone. He learned 72 changes and used a magic iron bar.
q: How many changes did Sun Wukong learn?

audioText: W: When did the movie start? M: By the time we got to the cinema, the movie had already started.
q: Did they arrive before or after the movie started?

audioText: W: Who was the king of the Greek gods? M: Zeus. He lived on Mount Olympus and could throw lightning.
q: What could Zeus throw?

audioText: W: Both Chinese and Greek stories are full of gods and heroes. M: Yes, ancient people used stories to explain the world around them.
q: Why did ancient people tell stories about gods and heroes?
options: To explain the world around them
explain: to explain the world around them.

audioText: W: How is the winter in Harbin? M: It lasts more than five months and the temperature often falls below zero.
q: How long does winter last in Harbin?

audioText: W: Is Guangzhou cold in winter? M: No, winter is warm and mild. It is seldom snowy there.
q: What is winter like in Guangzhou?

audioText: W: How much warmer is the Earth than 100 years ago? M: About one degree. It sounds small but makes a big difference.
q: How much warmer is the Earth than 100 years ago?

audioText: W: What is happening to glaciers? M: They are melting because of global warming. Sea levels are rising too.
q: What is happening to sea levels?

audioText: W: How long did English Week last? M: Five wonderful days, full of English everywhere in our school.
q: How many days did English Week last?

audioText: W: 'I am nervous,' she said. M: In reported speech, we say: She said she was nervous.
q: How do you report 'I am nervous' in the past?
explain: she was nervous — tense goes back.

audioText: W: What is the first tip for a good speech? M: Know your topic. Read a lot about it. The more you know, the more confident you are.
q: What is the first tip for a good speech?

audioText: W: How should you start a speech? M: Start with a story or a question. It catches the audience's attention right away.
q: How should you start a speech to catch attention?
options: With a story or a question
explain: with a story or a question.

audioText: W: How often do you visit the Sunshine Home? M: Every second Saturday. We help the elderly with cleaning and reading.
q: How often do the volunteers visit?

audioText: W: Why do you volunteer? M: I come to help the elderly and to bring them joy. Helping others makes me happy too.
q: Why does the speaker volunteer?
options: To help the elderly and bring joy

audioText: W: Who is Madam Li? M: She's 92 and still teaches children. She learned by herself when she was young because there was no school.
q: How old is Madam Li?

audioText: W: What can we learn from volunteers? M: Giving to others brings meaning to life, no matter your age or background.
q: What does volunteering bring according to the speaker?

audioText: W: How do people greet each other without words? M: We smile, nod, or shake hands. Body language speaks louder than words sometimes.
q: How do people communicate without words?

audioText: W: Does thumbs up mean the same everywhere? M: No, in China it means 'good', but in some countries it can be rude.
q: Does thumbs up mean the same in all countries?

audioText: W: Why did you smile at the stranger? M: I smiled because I wanted to be friendly. A smile can break any wall.
q: Why did the speaker smile?
options: Because he wanted to be friendly
explain: because I wanted to be friendly.

audioText: W: What linkers can join two ideas? M: Use 'because' for reasons, 'so' for results, and 'but' for contrast.
q: Which linker shows result?

audioText: W: How old was your grandma when she learned paper-cutting? M: She was eight. Her own grandmother taught her the skill.
q: At what age did Grandma learn paper-cutting?

audioText: W: Do you still cut paper every day? M: I used to, but now I only do it on weekends. I'm used to spending more time with family.
q: Does the speaker still cut paper every day?

audioText: W: Why should we save traditional skills? M: They carry our history and culture. If we don't pass them on, they will disappear.
q: What will happen if we don't save traditional skills?

audioText: W: What traditional skills do you know? M: Suzhou embroidery, Jingdezhen porcelain, Weifang kites and Hangzhou tea — all famous in China.
q: Which city is famous for porcelain?

audioText: W: What can your robot do? M: Buddy can sing, tell jokes, answer questions and even dance. He is like a real friend.
q: What can Buddy the robot do?

audioText: W: What will happen if I press this button? M: If you press the button, the robot will start singing your favourite song.
q: What will happen if you press the button?

audioText: W: Where do robots work nowadays? M: In factories they build cars, in hospitals they help with surgery, and at home they clean floors.
q: Where do robots help with surgery?

audioText: W: Will robots take all our jobs? M: Not all. Robots can do repetitive work, but humans are still needed for creative and caring jobs.
q: What jobs still need humans according to the speaker?

audioText: W: Where is Sanjiangyuan? M: In Qinghai province. It is the source of three great rivers — the Yangtze, Yellow and Lancang.
q: How many great rivers start from Sanjiangyuan?

audioText: W: How long has the reserve been there? M: It has been protected since 2005 — that's for over twenty years now.
q: Since when has the reserve been protected?

audioText: W: What endangered animals live in Sanjiangyuan? M: Snow leopards and Tibetan antelopes. They are still rare but their numbers are growing.
q: Which animals are mentioned as endangered?

audioText: W: Can children help save wildlife? M: Yes! Learn about endangered animals, share the knowledge, and don't buy wild animal products.
q: What is one way children can help wildlife?

audioText: W: What did your grandfather teach you about gardening? M: Three secrets — plant at the right depth, give enough sunlight, and be patient.
q: How many gardening secrets did the grandfather teach?

audioText: W: Did you plant those flowers yourself? M: Yes, I planted them myself. Gardening is my favourite hobby now.
q: Who planted the flowers?

audioText: W: Can plants really cure illnesses? M: Yes, for thousands of years people have used plants as medicine. Ginger helps colds, mint helps the stomach.
q: What plant helps with colds?

audioText: W: Who was Li Shizhen? M: A great ancient Chinese doctor. He travelled across China to study plants and wrote a famous medical book.
q: What did Li Shizhen do?
options: He studied plants and wrote a medical book
explain: studied plants and wrote a medical book.

audioText: W: When did humans first land on the moon? M: In 1969. Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the moon.
q: When did humans first land on the moon?

audioText: W: Is there water on the moon? M: No, there is no air, no water and no sound. It is completely silent.
q: What does the moon have none of?
explain: no air, no water and no sound.

audioText: W: Will people live on the moon one day? M: It might be possible. Scientists are drawing plans for moon bases underground.
q: Where might the moon base be built?

audioText: W: Why build the moon base underground? M: To protect from radiation and extreme temperatures. The moon's surface is very dangerous.
q: Why build the moon base underground?

audioText: W: What did your school do for Green Month? M: Each class had a green idea. Our class chose Zero Plastic Lunch.
q: What idea did the speaker's class choose?

audioText: W: I always forget my reusable bag. M: You'd better bring one, or you'll have to pay for a plastic bag at the shop.
q: What will happen if you don't bring a reusable bag?
explain: you'll pay for a plastic bag.

audioText: W: Which is stronger — 'should' or 'had better'? M: 'Had better' is stronger. It suggests a warning or negative result if you don't do it.
q: Which suggestion is stronger?

audioText: W: Can small steps really change the world? M: Yes! The biggest journey starts with a single step. Use a reusable bottle, walk more, recycle.
q: What is the first small step suggested?

audioText: W: Who was Confucius? M: He was one of the wisest men in Chinese history, who taught kindness and respect over 2,500 years ago.
q: When did Confucius live?

audioText: W: What is Confucius' most famous teaching? M: 'Do not do to others what you do not want done to yourself.'
q: What is Confucius' golden rule?
options: Treat others as you want to be treated
explain: do not do to others what you don't want done to yourself.

audioText: W: The students who wrote down Confucius' words became great teachers. M: Yes, they spread his wisdom across China.
q: Who spread Confucius' wisdom?

audioText: W: Confucius never wrote a long book. What we know comes from his students' notes. M: That shows he was a great teacher, not just a writer.
q: How do we know about Confucius' ideas?
explain: his students wrote down what he said.

audioText: W: What did Edison say about genius? M: 'Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.'
q: What percentage did Edison say was hard work?

audioText: W: How many times did Edison fail? M: Thousands of times, but he never gave up. Each failure taught him something new.
q: What did Edison do when he failed?

audioText: W: Who was Marie Curie? M: A woman whose curiosity was stronger than any rule. She discovered two new elements.
q: How many elements did Curie discover?
explain: two new elements — radium and polonium.

audioText: W: Is the lab where Edison worked still there? M: Yes, it has been turned into a museum. You can visit the place where history was made.
q: What happened to Edison's lab?

audioText: W: What did your survey find? M: Three problems — too much rubbish, noise pollution, and not enough green space.
q: How many problems did the survey find?

audioText: W: The noise was so loud that we couldn't study. M: Yes, it was too loud to concentrate on anything.
q: Why couldn't the students study?
explain: so loud that we couldn't study.

audioText: W: What are the smaller worries in big cities? M: Street noise, food waste and old buildings — problems people often ignore.
q: What is one 'smaller worry' in big cities?

audioText: W: The problem is too serious to ignore any longer. M: Yes, it's so serious that we must act now before it's too late.
q: What must they do about the problem?

audioText: W: What is the school campaign about? M: 'Small Steps, Big Planet.' Each class must choose one green action for a whole month.
q: How long must each class do the green action?

audioText: W: It is small actions that make a big difference. M: Exactly. It was students who started this campaign.
q: Who started the campaign?

audioText: W: What can cities do to be greener? M: Copenhagen uses bikes, Singapore has vertical gardens, and some cities turn waste into energy.
q: What does Singapore do to be green?

audioText: W: Can one city solve climate change alone? M: No, but every city's experiment teaches the world something new.
q: What can one city contribute according to the speaker?

audioText: W: What films did you watch? M: One about a dancer and a documentary about climate change. Both were worth watching.
q: What was the second film about?

audioText: W: Where are most films made? M: Many films are made in Hollywood, but great films are also made in China, India and Europe.
q: Where are 'many films made' according to the speaker?
explain: also made in China, India and Europe.

audioText: W: When was the first Chinese film made? M: In 1905. It was only about ten minutes long and was shot in a small photo studio.
q: How long was the first Chinese film?

audioText: W: Every year, film awards are given to the best actors. M: Yes, the Oscars have been held since 1929.
q: Since when have the Oscars been held?

audioText: W: How was the concert? M: Amazing! I have never been to such a wonderful concert in my whole life.
q: How did the speaker feel about the concert?
explain: amazing, never been to such a wonderful concert.

audioText: W: Have all the tickets been sold? M: Yes, all tickets have been sold. The concert is completely full.
q: What happened to the tickets?

audioText: W: How has entertainment changed? M: From street shows to TV, Internet and VR. The show changes, but the joy stays the same.
q: What has stayed the same despite changes?

audioText: W: The concert has been held in this stadium for ten years. M: It must have become a tradition by now.
q: How long has the concert been held in the stadium?

audioText: W: How deep is the deep sea you explored? M: 10,000 metres below the surface. It's completely dark and the pressure is extreme.
q: How deep were they?

audioText: W: 'The sea is mysterious,' the scientist said. M: So he said that the sea was mysterious.
q: What did the scientist say in reported speech?

audioText: W: 'What lives down there?' she asked. M: She asked what lived down there. We still don't fully know.
q: Do we fully know what lives in the deep sea?

audioText: W: Humans always look up at space and down into the ocean. M: Yes, curiosity drives us to explore both ends of our world.
q: What drives humans to explore?

audioText: W: What can your robot Aido do? M: He can greet me, learn my name and remember my preferences. AI is getting really smart.
q: What can Aido remember?

audioText: W: He left early — his coat is gone. M: He must have left in a hurry. Perhaps he forgot something important.
q: What does 'must have left' express?
options: A logical conclusion about the past
explain: logical conclusion about a past event.

audioText: W: You should have told me earlier about the meeting! M: I'm sorry. I might have forgotten to send the message.
q: What does 'should have told' express?
explain: regret — you didn't tell me but you should have.

audioText: W: What would people 200 years ago think of smartphones? M: They would have thought it was magic. Science keeps surprising us.
q: What would people 200 years ago have thought of smartphones?
options: They would think it was magic
explain: would have thought it was magic.

audioText: W: What year is Anna's diary from? M: 2049. She lives on Mars, at Station Hope-1. The sky there is a dusty orange-pink.
q: What colour is the Martian sky?

audioText: W: What will you be doing at this time tomorrow? M: I will be travelling to Mars! The journey takes about seven months.
q: What tense is 'will be travelling'?

audioText: W: Why do we explore Mars? M: It teaches us to live with fewer resources, drives new technology, and gives humanity a backup plan.
q: How many reasons for Mars exploration are mentioned?

audioText: W: Is Mars exploration worth the money? M: Yes, the technology we develop for Mars also helps us solve problems on Earth.
q: How does Mars technology help Earth?
explain: technology for Mars also helps Earth.

audioText: W: At what age did Helen Keller lose her sight and hearing? M: Only 19 months old. But she never gave up on learning.
q: When did Helen Keller lose her sight and hearing?

audioText: W: Who taught Helen to communicate? M: Anne Sullivan, her teacher. By the time she arrived, Helen had already been in darkness for years.
q: Which tense shows action BEFORE Sullivan arrived?

audioText: W: Are great people only famous names in books? M: No, many ordinary heroes live on our own streets — teachers, volunteers, neighbours.
q: According to the speaker, where can we find great people?
explain: ordinary heroes on our own streets.

audioText: W: What was Helen's message to young people? M: The best things in life cannot be seen or touched — they are felt with the heart.
q: How are the best things in life felt according to Helen?

audioText: W: How long is the journey across Asia? M: Ten days, starting from Beijing and visiting the most amazing places on the largest continent.
q: How many days is the journey?

audioText: W: Which is more modern, Tokyo or Beijing? M: Tokyo is more modern in technology, but Beijing has more ancient history.
q: How do you say 'more modern' in the comparative?

audioText: W: What four Asian cities did you visit? M: Tokyo, Singapore, Shanghai and Mumbai — each shows a different face of modern Asia.
q: Which city is NOT mentioned?

audioText: W: Asia is the largest continent with both ancient temples and modern wonders. M: That's what makes it the most fascinating place to explore.
q: What makes Asia fascinating?
options: Both ancient temples and modern wonders

audioText: W: What day is it today? M: World Environment Day. We have three guests from different parts of the world.
q: What day is being celebrated?

audioText: W: If we protect our forests, what will happen? M: If we protect them, the Earth will be healthier for our children.
q: What type of conditional is this?

audioText: W: Is Bhutan really carbon-negative? M: Yes, it's the only country in the world that absorbs more carbon than it produces.
q: What is special about Bhutan?

audioText: W: If every country were carbon-negative, climate change would slow down. M: That's a dream worth fighting for.
q: What type of conditional is 'If every country were...'?

audioText: W: Why do people set off firecrackers during Spring Festival? M: To scare away evil spirits and welcome a lucky new year.
q: Why are firecrackers set off?

audioText: W: How long have you celebrated Spring Festival? M: I have celebrated it since I was born. It's the most important festival for us.
q: Since when has the speaker celebrated Spring Festival?

audioText: W: What do dumplings symbolise? M: Wealth and family reunion. That's why we always eat them on New Year's Eve.
q: What do dumplings symbolise?

audioText: W: Name four world festivals. M: Songkran in Thailand, Diwali in India, Carnival in Brazil, and Mid-Autumn Festival in China.
q: Which festival is celebrated in Brazil?

audioText: W: How was your first week in China, Marco? M: Crazy and wonderful, but also a little confusing. Everything is so different!
q: How did Marco describe his first week?

audioText: W: What does 'When in Rome' mean? M: It means when you visit a new place, follow the local customs and traditions.
q: What does 'When in Rome' mean?

audioText: W: She was tired; however, she kept working. M: 'However' shows contrast. 'Therefore' would show result.
q: What does 'however' show?

audioText: W: What is the first tip for travellers? M: Observe before you act. Watch how locals behave, and follow their lead.
q: What is the first tip for travellers?

audioText: W: Does a poem always have to rhyme? M: No, sometimes it doesn't. Poetry is like painting with words.
q: What is poetry compared to?

audioText: W: 'Her voice is like music' — is this a simile or metaphor? M: It's a simile because it uses 'like'. A metaphor would say 'Her voice is music.'
q: Which uses 'like' or 'as' — simile or metaphor?

audioText: W: How old is Chinese poetry? M: More than 3,000 years old. The Tang Dynasty was its golden age.
q: Which dynasty was the golden age of Chinese poetry?

audioText: W: Why is Li Bai read worldwide? M: His poems express universal feelings — loneliness, friendship and wonder — that cross all cultures.
q: Why is Li Bai still popular worldwide?

audioText: W: Who is the most famous English playwright? M: Shakespeare. His plays explore love, power, jealousy and human nature.
q: What themes does Shakespeare explore?
explain: love, power, jealousy and human nature.

audioText: W: 'I have never seen such a play,' she said. M: In reported speech: She said she had never seen such a play.
q: How does 'have never seen' change in reported speech?
explain: had never seen — present perfect → past perfect.

audioText: W: Name a book that changed the world. M: The Analects of Confucius and Darwin's Origin of Species — both challenged old ways of thinking.
q: What do these books have in common?
options: They challenged old ways of thinking

audioText: W: What power do great books have? M: They can change how we think and shape the course of history. That's why we still read them centuries later.
q: Why do we still read great books centuries later?
options: They change how we think and shape history
explain: change how we think and shape history.
